scenes.title: Serialization & Schema Registry
scenes.subtitle: Enforcing structure with Avro and Protobuf
scenes.narration: Serialization turns objects into bytes for Kafka, and a schema registry keeps those bytes structured and compatible over time.

scenes.title: Why Schemas Matter
bullets: Kafka stores raw bytes with no notion of structure
Schemas give producers and consumers a shared contract
Avro and Protobuf are compact and typed
The registry validates and versions each schema
scenes.narration: Kafka itself stores only raw bytes and has no idea what they mean. Schemas provide a shared contract so producers and consumers agree on the shape of the data. Avro and Protobuf serialize that data into compact, strongly typed binary formats. A schema registry stores each schema centrally, validates messages against it, and tracks versions as the schema evolves.

scenes.title: How the Registry Fits In
steps: Message carries the id, not the full schema
Consumer fetches schema by id to decode
scenes.narration: The workflow keeps messages small. The producer registers its schema, and the registry returns a compact schema id. Each message then carries just that id plus the encoded data, not the full schema. The consumer reads the id, fetches the matching schema from the registry, and uses it to decode the bytes correctly.

scenes.title: Compatibility Modes
scenes.narration: The registry enforces compatibility rules as schemas change. Backward compatibility means a new schema can still read data written with the old one, so you upgrade consumers first. Forward compatibility means an old schema can read data written with a new one, so you upgrade producers first. Full compatibility satisfies both, which is the safest default for evolving contracts.

scenes.title: Producing with Avro
scenes.code:
from confluent_kafka.schema_registry import SchemaRegistryClient
from confluent_kafka.schema_registry.avro import AvroSerializer

sr = SchemaRegistryClient({'url': 'http://localhost:8081'})
schema = '{"type":"record","name":"Order","fields":[{"name":"id","type":"int"}]}'
serializer = AvroSerializer(sr, schema)

producer.produce(
    topic='orders',
    value=serializer({'id': 101}, ctx),
)
scenes.narration: This producer connects to the schema registry running on port 8081. It defines an Avro record schema for an order with a typed integer id. The AvroSerializer registers that schema and encodes each record into compact binary, prefixed with the schema id. On the other side, a matching deserializer will fetch the schema by id and reconstruct the object safely.

scenes.text: Set a compatibility policy and treat schema changes like API changes. This lets producers and consumers evolve independently without breaking each other.
scenes.narration: As a best practice, set a compatibility policy and treat every schema change like an API change. This lets producers and consumers evolve independently without breaking one another.
